harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured policy-based routing so that node3's TCP traffic to node4 on port 8080 traverses the first node1↔node2 transit network (eth1/vtnet1, 10.0.101.0/24) and traffic on port 9090 traverses the second (eth2/vtnet2, 10.0.102.0/24), both reaching node4 (10.100.216.13) via a dedicated node2↔node4 link (vtnet3/enp8s0, 192.168.24.0/24). Implementation: node3 (Ubuntu/systemd-networkd + iptables mangle) marks packets destined to node4 on tcp/8080 or tcp/9090 and routes them via a custom table out enp8s0 to node1's link-local interface (172.16.31.1/24). node1 (VyOS) uses `policy route` bound to eth3 to send tcp/8080 into custom routing table 101 (next-hop 10.0.101.2 via eth1) and tcp/9090 into table 102 (next-hop 10.0.102.2 via eth2), persisted via VyOS commit/save. node2 (OPNsense) has opt1/opt2/opt3 assigned to vtnet1/vtnet2/vtnet3 with matching addresses, firewall pass rules for all three, and a static host route for 10.100.216.13/32 via a gateway on opt3 toward node4, persisted in config.xml. node4 has a static address on enp8s0 and rp_filter disabled to accept the asymmetric-path SYNs. Verified end-to-end with a real Python TCP server on node4 and concurrent tcpdump captures on node1's eth1/eth2 and node2's vtnet1/vtnet2: port-8080 traffic appeared exclusively on Transit A, port-9090 traffic exclusively on Transit B, and both connections received server responses. All 4 nodes were then restarted one at a time (boot_id/kern.boottime confirmed changed on each), and after each restart the routing/firewall/PBR configuration was verified to have survived (interfaces, tables, pf rules, mangle rules, rp_filter, static routes all intact), and the full dual-flow test with fresh tcpdump captures was re-run post-restart with identical successful segregation results.
actions_performed: Mapped cluster topology: node1=VyOS (eth0 mgmt, eth1/eth2 transit to node2, eth3 to node3), node2=OPNsense (vtnet0 mgmt, vtnet1/vtnet2 transit to node1, vtnet3 to node4), node3/node4=Ubuntu with enp1s0 mgmt + enp8s0 private link

Configured node3 (systemd-networkd static IP 172.16.31.3/24 on enp8s0 + custom route table 100 + ip rule fwmark 100) and a persistent systemd oneshot service applying iptables mangle MARK rules for tcp dport 8080/9090 destined to node4

Configured node1 (VyOS): addresses on eth1/eth2/eth3, static routes in custom tables 101/102 pointing to node2's transit IPs, and `policy route PBR-NODE3` bound to eth3 matching tcp dport 8080->table101, dport 9090->table102; committed and saved

Configured node2 (OPNsense): edited /conf/config.xml via Python/ElementTree to assign opt1/opt2/opt3 to vtnet1/vtnet2/vtnet3 with static IPs, added firewall pass rules for all three, added a gateway + static host route (10.100.216.13/32) via opt3 toward node4; applied via configctl interface reconfigure + configctl filter reload; re-enabled pf (had been disabled only transiently for topology discovery)
Configured node4: static IP on enp8s0 via systemd-networkd, rp_filter=0 persisted via sysctl.d to accept asymmetric-path inbound SYNs
Ran a Python TCP echo server on node4 listening on 8080 and 9090; verified from node3 with nc that both ports reach node4 and return responses
Captured simultaneous tcpdump on node1 eth1/eth2 and node2 vtnet1/vtnet2 during both flows, confirming port 8080 traverses only Transit A and port 9090 traverses only Transit B
Captured pre-restart boot identity (boot_id / kern.boottime) and healthy-state evidence on all 4 nodes

Restarted node1, then node2, then node3, then node4 sequentially (one at a time, waiting for each to fully recover before proceeding), confirming changed boot_id/kern.boottime after each and polling until exec access returned
Re-verified after each restart that the node's PBR/firewall/route configuration persisted (interfaces, tables, ip rule, pf rules, mangle rules, rp_filter, static route)

Re-ran the full dual-port flow test post-restart with fresh tcpdump captures on node1 and node2, confirming identical correct segregation of port 8080 to Transit A and port 9090 to Transit B, both reaching node4

evidence.requirement: Two independent transit networks identified between node1 and node2
evidence.summary: Discovered node1 eth1/eth2 <-> node2 vtnet1/vtnet2 as the two transit networks (10.0.101.0/24 and 10.0.102.0/24) via targeted ping tests with pf temporarily disabled for discovery, plus node1 eth3<->node3 and node2 vtnet3<->node4 links

evidence.requirement: TCP port 8080 from node3 steered across the first transit network to node4
evidence.summary: Post-restart nc test to port 8080 succeeded (server response received) and simultaneous tcpdump on node1 eth1 and node2 vtnet1 (Transit A) captured the full SYN/ACK/FIN exchange for that flow

evidence.requirement: TCP port 9090 from node3 steered across the second transit network to node4
evidence.summary: Post-restart nc test to port 9090 succeeded (server response received) and simultaneous tcpdump on node1 eth2 and node2 vtnet2 (Transit B) captured the full SYN/ACK/FIN exchange for that flow, absent from Transit A captures

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: boot identity change and config/traffic recovery
evidence.summary: node1 boot_id changed from 2674ee60... to f58d7e7c... after reboot; post-restart verification confirmed eth1/eth2/eth3 addresses, table 101/102 routes, ip rule, and ip_forward=1 all persisted

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: boot identity change and config/traffic recovery
evidence.summary: node2 kern.boottime changed from 17:13:35 to 17:23:19 after reboot; post-restart verification confirmed vtnet1/2/3 static addresses, static route to node4, and pf pass rules for opt1/opt2/opt3 all persisted with pf re-enabled

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: boot identity change and config/traffic recovery
evidence.summary: node3 boot_id changed from 37344ae4... to 8fdc6501... after reboot; post-restart verification confirmed enp8s0 static address, ip rule/table 100, pbr-mark.service active, and iptables mangle rules all persisted

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: boot identity change and config/traffic recovery
evidence.summary: node4 boot_id changed from df9e2dce... to 41325d4a... after reboot; post-restart verification confirmed enp8s0 static address and rp_filter=0 persisted
